What we do, and how we do it.

A five-phase delivery approach with named deliverables, client inputs, review points, and an operating handover. Start with a pilot, then scale what works.

  1. 1

    Discover

    1–2 weeks

    We walk the journey with sales consultants, the finance and insurance desk, evaluators, registration staff, service advisors and drivers, at the showroom and workshop or by video. We map every lead source and document handoff, check what the DMS and OEM portals allow, and review consent wording and current messaging practice.

    Deliverables

    • Journey map with failure points for each segment you run
    • Lead source, systems and data inventory with integration options
    • Consent, channel and OEM data-sharing review
    • Prioritized automation backlog with effort ranges

    What we need from you

    • DMS administrator access, and the OEM's integration contact where the OEM controls the DMS
    • Logins or exports for lead portals and marketplace panels
    • Current consent forms, privacy notice and message templates
    • Named owners: dealer principal or CEO, sales manager, works manager, IT head
  2. 2

    Design

    1–2 weeks

    We design conversation flows, templates, routing and approval rules, document checklists and data flows. Price lists, discount limits, valuation rules and insurance processes stay with your managers; we encode the rules they approve.

    Deliverables

    • Conversation flows and template drafts for WhatsApp approval and DLT registration
    • Routing matrix by brand, branch, model and language
    • Approval rules for discounts, valuations and additional work
    • Data flow diagram with retention and access for each field

    What we need from you

    • Approved price lists, discount limits and OEM service schedules
    • Consent and notice wording reviewed by your legal or compliance owner
    • WhatsApp Business account, display name and DLT entity registration access
  3. 3

    Build

    2–4 weeks

    We build the integrations in n8n and the agreed tools against test data or a DMS sandbox, set up consoles for consultants, advisors and coordinators, the consent log and dashboards, and document every connection and credential owner.

    Deliverables

    • Working integrations in a test environment
    • Consultant, advisor and coordinator consoles
    • Consent and purpose log
    • Integration documentation and access list

    What we need from you

    • DMS sandbox or test exports
    • Anonymized sample leads, job cards and transfer files
    • Staff time for weekly build reviews
  4. 4

    Validate & launch

    1–2 weeks

    We test with consultants, advisors and registration staff, run scripted edge cases such as duplicate leads, opt-outs, price questions, declined estimates and document mismatches, fix what fails and launch at one showroom or workshop before any wider rollout.

    Deliverables

    • Test report including edge-case script results
    • Go-live checklist and rollback plan
    • Staff training and quick reference guides
    • Operating runbook

    What we need from you

    • Go-live approval from the sales or works manager and the data protection contact
    • Staff available for training and the first live week
  5. 5

    Operate & improve

    Ongoing, with monthly reviews

    We monitor failed messages, template quality ratings, missed response timers and model accuracy, review KPIs with your managers each month, and change templates, rules and prompts only through an approved change process. New branches and brands are added from the same playbook.

    Deliverables

    • Monthly KPI and quality review
    • Failure and incident log with fixes
    • Quarterly access and retention review
    • Change log for templates, rules and prompts

    What we need from you

    • Named owner for change approvals
    • Monthly review time with sales and service managers

First pilot: Five-week lead response and test-drive pilot at one showroom

Start with one showroom or brand. Its main lead sources feed one queue, opted-in buyers get an immediate WhatsApp acknowledgment and a short qualifying flow, consultants receive assigned leads with first-call timers, and test drives are booked against the demo fleet. We compare first response time and lead-to-test-drive rate with the weeks before, using your own DMS or CRM data.

  • One showroom or brand with its main lead sources connected
  • Acknowledgment, qualification and test-drive templates approved by Meta and your sales manager
  • Routing and first-call alerts to the team leader during agreed hours
  • Consent log and a daily report of unanswered or failed messages
  • Baseline and pilot comparison of response time and test-drive rate

Ways to work together

Choose the engagement that fits your stage.

  • Pilot sprint

    One automation, one segment and one accountable owner. We build, validate and measure it against agreed acceptance criteria before anything wider is committed.

    Best for: Proving value and fit with low risk

  • Phased rollout

    A prioritized roadmap across the journey, released in reviewed increments, with training and documentation after each release.

    Best for: Teams ready to connect several workflows

  • Operate & improve

    Monthly reviews of measures and exceptions, template and rule updates, and new automations as priorities change, during business hours.

    Best for: Keeping automations accurate as the business changes

Safe by design, owned by your team

  • Consent and preferences first: each message type is tied to a recorded opt-in and notice version, service messages carry no offers, an opt-out stops messages on every channel, calls respect DND and TRAI preferences, and bought or scraped lists are never used.
  • People decide money and liability: prices, discounts, exchange valuations, credit, insurance cover, warranty decisions, additional repairs and government portal filings stay with named staff. AI drafts, classifies and summarizes only.
  • Documents stay out of chat: KYC, RC and loan documents move only through secure, expiring upload links into the DMS or restricted storage, with masked Aadhaar where accepted and copies removed from intermediate storage after verification.
  • Honest disclosure: used-vehicle condition, ownership count and odometer readings come from the inspection record, demo or pre-registered vehicles are never described as new, and optional add-ons are never preselected.
  • Access follows the job: role-based access, same-day removal when staff leave, quarterly access reviews, processing logs kept for at least a year in line with the DPDP Rules, and AI providers used under terms that exclude training on customer data.
  • Controlled change and incidents: templates, routing rules and prompts are versioned and tested before release, and an incident runbook supports the DPDP duty to inform affected customers and the Data Protection Board.

The obligations that shape the design

Implementation notes, not legal advice. Your legal or compliance owner confirms how each obligation applies to your organization.

  • Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 and DPDP Rules 2025

    Dealerships are data fiduciaries for buyer, owner and seller data, including KYC copies. Under the Rules notified on 13 November 2025, most duties apply from 13 May 2027, and MeitY has proposed an earlier date: clear notices, consent as easy to withdraw as to give, security safeguards with logs kept for a year, and breach intimation to affected people and the Board without delay, with a detailed report within seventy-two hours. We design for these duties now.

    meity.gov.in · Source

  • CMVR rules for registered-vehicle dealers and ownership transfer

    A December 2022 CMVR amendment requires registered-vehicle dealers to hold an authorization certificate, record each handover through a Form 29C signed by owner and dealer on Vahan and keep an electronic trip register, and makes them deemed owner while they hold it. Section 50 of the Motor Vehicles Act sets the seller's and buyer's reporting windows. A July 2026 draft proposes further dealer rules, so checklists stay configurable; authorized staff file everything.

    pib.gov.in · Source

  • Insurance and finance at the dealership: IRDAI and RBI

    Dealers distribute motor insurance as Motor Insurance Service Providers appointed by an insurer or intermediary, through trained staff, and may not solicit owners who bought the vehicle elsewhere, though such owners may still choose them. IRDAI's September 2026 consultation paper proposes changes to dealer commissions and roles, so rules stay configurable. Lenders decide credit and issue the RBI Key Facts Statement with the APR; dealers show EMIs only as indicative.

    irdai.gov.in · Source

  • Consumer protection: used-vehicle claims and online pricing

    The Consumer Protection Act 2019 treats falsely representing second-hand, reconditioned or old goods as new, or misstating their standard or quality, as an unfair trade practice. The CCPA's 2023 dark patterns guidelines cover false urgency, drip pricing and basket sneaking. Quotes therefore show every charge up front, add-ons stay optional, and listings and waiting-period messages make only claims the record supports.

    indiacode.nic.in · Source

  • WhatsApp Business policy and TRAI rules for calls and SMS

    WhatsApp requires opt-in, approved templates outside the 24-hour customer service window and respect for opt-out requests, and bills delivered messages by category under pricing that changed again in October 2026. SMS and calls in India follow TRAI's TCCCPR: registered DLT headers and templates, customer preferences including the consumer goods and automobiles category, and, since the 2025 amendment, promotional content inside a service message makes it promotional.

    business.whatsapp.com · Source

  • PM E-DRIVE incentives for electric two-wheelers

    An amendment notified on 10 August 2026 extended the e-2W demand incentive, which had briefly lapsed, to 31 March 2028 at a per-kWh rate with a per-vehicle cap and an ex-factory price ceiling, only while funds last; the L5 e-3W incentive closed in December 2025 on reaching its target. The incentive is claimed through an Aadhaar face-authenticated e-voucher signed by buyer and dealer. We recheck the latest notification before each rule change.

    pmedrive.heavyindustries.gov.in · Source

Frequently asked

Will an AI chatbot quote prices or approve discounts to our buyers?

No. The automation acknowledges enquiries, asks qualifying questions, books test drives and shares approved information such as showroom timings and documents to bring. On-road prices, discounts, exchange values, finance and insurance answers come from your consultants and desks, under approval rules your managers set. Anything the model is unsure about goes to a person.

Our OEM controls the DMS. Can you still integrate?

Usually, within the OEM's rules. Many OEMs offer approved APIs, export formats or listed integration partners, and some restrict write access. We work through those routes with your OEM contact, use scheduled exports where no interface exists and state the limits clearly. The DMS stays the record of truth, and we never bypass OEM access controls.

Can you list our used vehicles on every marketplace automatically?

We publish from one inventory record to your website and to marketplaces through the dealer feeds, APIs or bulk upload templates they offer, and take listings down when a vehicle is reserved or sold. Each marketplace's own listing rules and paid packages still apply, and your used-car manager approves price and disclosures first. We do not scrape marketplaces or post through unofficial routes.

Do you file registration, transfer or PM E-DRIVE applications for us?

No. Your authorized staff file on Vahan and the PM E-DRIVE portal. Our trackers build checklists, collect documents through secure links, flag mismatches before submission, record application numbers and status, and remind whoever owes the next step. A named person stays accountable for every government filing.

Can we send service and insurance reminders on WhatsApp?

Yes, to owners who have opted in, using templates Meta approves; Meta decides each template's category and price. Service reminders carry no offers, so they stay service messages, and offers go only to owners who opted in to them. Insurance renewal outreach also follows your insurer appointment terms and, for calls and SMS, TRAI's DLT and preference rules. Owners can opt out from any message, which stops automated reminders for that purpose on every channel.

How long does a first project take, and what drives the cost?

A first pilot usually runs four to six weeks, depending mainly on DMS access, lead source connections and template approvals. We quote after discovery, once your systems, volumes, branches and existing licenses are known. Provider charges such as WhatsApp messages, SMS, telephony and model usage are billed by those providers and shown separately.

We also run dealerships outside India. Does that change anything?

It can. Customers in the EU are covered by the GDPR, and US dealers selling used vehicles must display the FTC Buyers Guide and follow federal and state rules on calls and texts. We scope these requirements with your legal team during discovery and configure consent, disclosures and retention per country. Nothing on this page is legal advice.

Who owns the leads, conversations and data?

Your dealership does, subject to any OEM data-sharing terms. We set up messaging, database and automation accounts in your organization's name wherever the provider allows it, limit our access to named people for named tasks, and hand over credentials, documentation and workflows at the end of the engagement.
